messages:
felix: FYI observed spike in mTLS handshake errors from eu-west services to acme-proxy around 2025-06-07T09:12Z. Canary saw ~4% failures.
tara: logs? sample error looks like "no shared application protocol (ALPN)" during TLS handshake, which is odd for our internal proxies.
kms-audit-bot: ALERT: KMS Decrypt on key=acme-keystore-eu at 2025-06-07T09:08Z by principal=svc:rotator-eu:ephemeral-test-2025-06-07 — issuer metadata mismatch detected.
harpreet: could be a cert chain swap — that would cause ALPN negotiation to fail if client expectation (h2,http/1.1) isn't met because server presented wrong cert type.
eng-infra: we pushed a terraform patch yesterday that added `google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding` for serviceAccount:ci-runner@infra.example.com with note "temp: cross-region keystore test". Did we intend that to be live?
tara: checking KMS audit: decrypts at 09:07 and 09:08 by ephemeral rotator and ci-runner. Need to map which CSR those decrypts correspond to.
felix: grabbing proxy logs: `kubectl -n acme logs acme-proxy-eu | grep \"ALPN\" -A2` shows inbound from app-backend-eu with SNI=acme.internal and then `alert: presented cert issuer=fingerprint:abcd1234`. That fingerprint doesn't match our internal CA (expected ef56...).
harpreet: that explains it. Clients reject because cert chain not anchored to our CA and ALPN negotiation falls through. Who created the key binding? eng-infra?
eng-infra: that binding was created by infra-ci at 2025-06-06T23:50Z — job id 1224. It was tagged as a test but accidentally ran in prod. We're investigating why the pipeline targeted the prod KMS key.
kms-audit-bot: NOTE: Shadow certs were auto-provisioned by rotator for service=acme-proxy-eu at 2025-06-07T09:11Z. Promotion scheduled in 30 minutes unless rollback.
toncall-joe: oncall here. Immediate mit: 1) revoke the temp IAM binding 2) promote shadow certs if canary green 3) extend KMS audit retention to 60d for this key 4) rotate any CI tokens that could have been used. I'll drive mitigation.
tara: I've revoked the binding: `gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding projects/.../keys/acme-keystore-eu --member="serviceAccount:ci-runner@infra.example.com" --role="roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter"` — revoke logged.
felix: canary rotation in progress: `./rotator rotate --service acme-proxy-eu --use-shadow` — canary shows cert chain anchored to internal CA now, ALPN negotiation fixed on canary nodes.
harpreet: good. Forensics: grep KMS audit entries for decrypts between 2025-06-06T23:00Z and 2025-06-07T10:00Z, map to CSR IDs, and compare CSR signer_fingerprint -> certificate issuer. Also collect egress flows from rotator.
eng-infra: pipeline logs show job 1224 executed `terraform apply` with a feature flag `enable-keystore-crossbind`. The run was triggered by infra-ci (manual approval) but the approval UI showed "test" not "prod" — UX bug. We'll patch to block KMS IAM changes without peer review.
tara: add org-policy deny for roles/cloudkms.* on prod keys for non-privileged principals until we finish root cause. That prevents accidental binds.
oncall-joe: added temporary org-policy deny. Also opened ticket to rotate all client certs if we find evidence of external signing. For now, label as "potential supply-chain auth change".
felix: I ran a quick provenance search: only one cert was issued with fingerprint abcd1234 and it was not served widely — limited to a single node that hit the bad rotator run. Promoted shadow certs cleared the issue.
harpreet: still need to rotate CI tokens and examine if any external principal used KMS. If we see decrypt by non-org principal, escalate to P1.
eng-infra: infra-ci team will add stricter gating and an audit requirement for any terraform resource targeting kms keys. Also rolling back the feature flag in infra templates.
tara: documentation note: update runbook to include ALPN/fingerprint check in the rotator post-rotate validation. Add a post-rotate smoke that verifies ALPN advertised protocols and issuer fingerprint.
felix: I've extended KMS key logging retention and exported decrypt events to our sec-log BigQuery for faster analysis.
oncall-joe: legal & product notified as a precaution. If any customer certificate was touched we'll follow disclosure playbook.
harpreet: follow-up actions assigned: eng-infra -> fix pipeline UI + gate, ops -> rotate CI tokens, security -> provenance sweep across prod keys last 30 days.
tara: thanks team. If anyone sees the abcd1234 fingerprint elsewhere, ping this thread. I'll keep monitoring ALPN error rate. :mag_right:
